facts.statement: Brindabellaspis lived during the Early Devonian period.
When discovered in 1980, Brindabellaspis was initially classified as a Weejasperaspid acanthothoracid because of its anatomical similarities to other reef species.
facts.quote: When B. stensioi was first discovered in 1980, it was originally regarded as a Weejasperaspid acanthothoracid due to anatomical similarities with the other species found at the reef.

facts.statement: The dorsolaterally positioned eyes of Brindabellaspis suggest it lived a benthic lifestyle.
facts.quote: Regardless, its dorsolaterally positioned eyes are consistent with a benthic lifestyle.

facts.statement: Brindabellaspis was formerly considered part of the orders Acanthothoraci or Rhenanida but was eventually placed in its own order.
facts.quote: Antiguamente se consideraba parte del orden Acanthothoraci o Rhenanida pero al final se le colocó en su propio orden.

facts.statement: Brindabellaspis possesses an elongated ossification that flanks the serial bones supporting the lateral line, similar to maxillary placoderms.
facts.quote: También posee una osificación alargada que flanquea los huesos seriales que soportan la línea lateral siendo similar a los placodermos maxilares

facts.statement: The time range for Brindabellaspis is the Emsian stage, spanning from 410.62 to 393.47 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 393.47 million years ago)
